purpose: Compact cognitive recall markers for agents. Cues are stable English internal identifiers; user-language phrases must normalize to these identifiers through semantic adaptation, learned aliases, or route pattern storage.

cues.title: Internal contracts stay English
cues.summary: System internals use stable English symbols; user-language phrases normalize through semantic adaptation, learned aliases, or route pattern store.
cues.full_text: Internal SloplessCode contracts, intent types, cue ids, route ids, and workflow symbols stay in English. Do not hardcode user-language phrases into router code. User-language phrases, slang, typos, and keyboard-layout mistakes must be normalized into stable English canonical intents through semantic adaptation, learned aliases, or route pattern storage.

cues.title: Use public MCP for governed project context
cues.summary: Project memory, laws, task lifecycle, next-work selection, and handoff context should go through the public MCP surface.
cues.full_text: For SloplessCode/MnemoForge-backed work, use the public MCP surface as the canonical channel for governed project memory, laws, task lifecycle, next-work selection, and handoff context. Repository files, code search, and isolated tests remain normal implementation tools, but project-state decisions should not rely on direct API calls, ad-hoc Python scripts, shell history, or agent memory alone.

cues.title: Do not push data through code
cues.summary: Workflow meaning, routing examples, guardrails, and UI hints should live in specs or governed data; code should interpret them.
cues.full_text: Avoid the data-through-code architecture. Workflow states, allowed tools, required evidence, forbidden patterns, packet budgets, route examples, and guardrails should be represented as data/specs or governed memory where possible. Code should be a thin interpreter/executor rather than an accumulating if/else monolith.

cues.title: Resolve verification policy before live validation
cues.summary: Resolve the active project verification policy before touching external runtime; live validation needs explicit operator intent.
cues.full_text: Before live or external-runtime validation, resolve the active project verification policy and record evidence. Do not restart, smoke-test, or mutate external runtime merely to prove a code change unless the operator explicitly asks for live validation. Concrete contours such as Docker, host commands, wait windows, or service names are project knowledge and must come from governed project data, not this universal cue.

cues.title: Record progress after meaningful work
cues.summary: After a meaningful implementation, verification, commit, or handoff slice, record progress through the public MCP surface.
cues.full_text: After a meaningful implementation, verification, commit, publish, or handoff slice, record a durable progress checkpoint through the public MCP surface. Use record_progress when a task is not claimed or finish_task when closing a claimed task. Chat-only summaries and git commits are not sufficient project memory because the next agent must be able to resume from governed MCP state.

cues.title: Claim protects active work
cues.summary: Claim before implementation so other agents do not interfere and the system can checkpoint, recover, and finish your work.
cues.full_text: Claim is not permission to work; it is a coordination lock that protects your active task workspace from concurrent agents. Start or claim the task before implementation, keep the returned work_handle, record progress after meaningful slices, and finish with closeout evidence. If a lease conflict appears, assume it is protecting someone else's active work: recover with the valid work_handle, coordinate handoff, wait for TTL/release, or choose another task.

cues.title: Use semantic adaptation for user phrases
cues.summary: Recurring user wording, jargon, typos, and layout mistakes should become learned aliases, not source-code branches.
cues.full_text: Semantic adaptation is the learning contour for mapping user-specific language, jargon, recurring typos, and wrong-keyboard-layout phrases onto stable internal English concepts. Prefer storing learned mappings in governed data over adding language-specific conditionals.

cues.title: Use learned route patterns
cues.summary: Observed successful routes should reinforce canonical intent selection without expanding the public tool surface.
cues.full_text: The route pattern store records learned routing evidence and successful canonical intent choices. Use it to improve future routing without exposing more tools or hardcoding one-off phrases in source code.

cues.title: Localized hardcoding risk
cues.summary: Adding per-language phrase branches is an architecture risk; normalize to English canonical intents instead.
cues.full_text: Localized hardcoding is a P0 architecture risk: adding source-code branches for Russian, English, Spanish, or any other user language turns the system into a fragile phrase router. Normalize user wording into English canonical intents through learned data instead.
